summary: West Indies won the fifth and deciding T20 against England at the Brian Lara Stadium to take the series 3-2. After a record-smashing 267 two days earlier, England were bowled out for 132 and West Indies chased it down with four balls to spare, finishing with a six from Shai Hope. The match was a low-scoring contrast to the series' power hitting, and extended West Indies' home dominance over England.
one_line: West Indies beat England by chasing 133 in the decider, with Shai Hope's 43 and a closing six, to win the T20 series 3-2.
key_facts: West Indies won the T20 series 3-2 after winning the fifth and deciding match at the Brian Lara Stadium.
Shai Hope won the match for West Indies with a six, with four balls to spare, and made 43 off 43 balls.
England lost the toss, were put in to bat and scored only 132, less than half the 267 they made 48 hours earlier.
West Indies have now extended their supremacy over England at home to four series in three formats across nearly five years.
Gudakesh Motie dismissed Phil Salt for 38, ending Salt's run of absurd form, and also caught Livingstone.
England were 70 for four one ball into the ninth over after Jos Buttler fell to Oshane Thomas's catch off Jason Holder and Harry Brook was caught by Nicholas Pooran off Motie.
Liam Livingstone and Moeen Ali added 40 for the fifth wicket before Akeal Hosein, who took Will Jacks and Moeen, ended the stand.
England lost their last five wickets in 20 balls for 11 runs.
Akeal Hosein's four overs went for just 20 runs.
West Indies were 62 for three halfway through their chase, 15 runs fewer than England at the same point.
Adil Rashid, 35, rose to the top of the T20 bowling rankings for the first time, taking two wickets for 21.
Reece Topley took two wickets for 17 and called the game 'basically a final'; Topley and Sam Curran each conceded only two in their final overs.
